heading: Threat model
body: `bare-path` is one of the addons Bare compiles into its binary, so every Bare process has it, sealed or not, and it inherits [Bare's threat model](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md). The module's own [threat model](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-path/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md), added in v3.1.3, says where it sits in that one. It manipulates strings and touches no file system: joining a path does not open it. The one thing it reaches outside the process is the working directory, which `resolve()` reads and which tells sealed code a little about how the host file system is laid out. The risk is in the C that handles paths an attacker chose, where the Windows rules are the fiddly part. Code elsewhere that treats a path as safe because this module normalized it relies on the module agreeing with the OS, so output that differs from what the platform resolves the same input to is reportable.
